meta.title: Governed Agentic Process Modernization — Outcome Requirements
meta.status: Proposed requirements refactor, classification and scope changed; pending stakeholder acceptance
meta.note: Logical Design/Development, Control/Governance and Execution responsibilities; NOT three mandatory deployments

mandatory.title: Process semantics and definition validation
mandatory.requirement: Process or agent-driven behavior must have an inspectable, versioned definition or constrained execution contract; validate schemas, inputs, decision boundaries and expected transitions before publication.

mandatory.title: Bounded agent autonomy and risk controls
mandatory.requirement: Every agent task must have an approved goal, permitted tools/data, risk classification and limits on iterations, time and expenditure. AI cannot expand its own authority or bypass deterministic decisions and escalation controls.

mandatory.title: Durable execution and checkpoint recovery
mandatory.requirement: Committed process and agent progress must survive worker, node and storage failover, including waiting tasks and partial completion. Resume or retry must not repeat completed business effects.

mandatory.title: Durable triggers, timers and lifecycle
mandatory.requirement: Controlled API/event/schedule initiation, per-instance deadlines, timeouts, maximum lifetime, expiry and escalation must be recoverable after outage; duplicate timer delivery must not duplicate outcomes.

mandatory.title: Authorized human interaction
mandatory.requirement: When a process requires human action, task assignment, delegation, reassignment, approval/rejection, escalation and authorization must be durable and auditable. Separation of duties follows approved risk policy; consequential agents cannot self-approve.

mandatory.title: Events, business effects and compensation
mandatory.requirement: Correlate external events to the correct execution; external side effects must use idempotency or reconciliation, with visible compensation/manual-resolution on partial failures.

mandatory.title: Resilience under dependency failure and overload
mandatory.requirement: Apply bounded timeouts/retries, circuit breaking, backpressure and overload safety so committed work is neither silently lost nor duplicated.

mandatory.title: Backup, restore and disaster recovery
mandatory.requirement: Back up required process/agent state, activity history, configuration and audit evidence; prove restore against agreed RTO/RPO and without replaying completed irreversible effects.

mandatory.title: Version-safe in-flight work
mandatory.requirement: A running instance retains compatible or pinned process, policy, model and configuration semantics through new releases and rollback; no automatic migration is required.

mandatory.title: Governed publication and activation
mandatory.requirement: Definitions, prompts, models, tools and configuration are validated, authorized, versioned, integrity-checked, auditable and activatable/rollbackable under explicit release policy. No specific bundle format, signing transport or GitOps product is prescribed.

mandatory.title: Authentication, delegation and secret handling
mandatory.requirement: Authenticate users, agents and services; authorize the *effective* user and acting workload with scoped, short-lived credentials and no blanket token passthrough. Secrets are stored, rotated, revoked and reacquired on long waits.

mandatory.title: External policy and safe denial
mandatory.requirement: Business/security policy is enforced outside agents or at non-bypassable boundaries; unavailable mandatory policy decisions fail closed while safe recovery remains possible, and decisions are attributable and versioned.

mandatory.title: Data security, privacy and location
mandatory.requirement: Protect process state, task/history records, memory, prompts and audit data in transit and at rest with policy-based retention/erasure and permitted processing or storage locations for models, tools and backups.

mandatory.title: Untrusted inputs and optional code execution
mandatory.requirement: Validate model output, retrieved content and tool responses before consequential use. Agents cannot execute arbitrary generated code by default; if code execution is enabled, run it in an isolated resource-bounded sandbox with explicit grants.

mandatory.title: Auditability and AI decision provenance
mandatory.requirement: Maintain tamper-evident, queryable records of actors, decisions, state transitions, model/prompt/tool/policy versions and external effects, with sensitive payloads redacted or referenced according to retention rules.

mandatory.title: Observability and operational APIs
mandatory.requirement: Provide correlated traces/logs/metrics and authorized APIs to inspect, cancel, retry, pause and recover executions and human/agent tasks, without mandating a particular UI or database.

mandatory.title: AI change evaluation and model continuity
mandatory.requirement: Versioned quality, safety and security evaluations must gate material model/prompt/tool changes; model retirement and unavailable pinned models trigger controlled substitution, safe pause or approved fallback, never silent change.

mandatory.title: Supply-chain integrity and AI inventory
mandatory.requirement: Verify provenance of deployable code, packages, workflow definitions, models and tool registrations; keep a queryable inventory of agents, model bindings, prompts, tools and MCP servers with accountable owner, purpose, risk tier, version and status; permit only approved, inventoried artifacts and tool endpoints; and retain a traceable software/AI bill of materials as applicable.

mandatory.title: Agent context, memory and state governance
mandatory.requirement: Agent memory and checkpoints are scoped to the permitted user, instance and tenant, with data provenance, retention/erasure, bounded growth and sufficient state to recover or safely retry. Exact full/selective/compacted policy is configurable.

mandatory.title: Emergency containment and AI incident handling
mandatory.requirement: Authorized emergency controls stop/revoke selected agent, tool or model bindings within a defined bound, including handling of in-flight work, without relying on an AI assistant or unavailable authoring service. AI incidents are recorded, classified by severity, reported where the applicable profile requires, and reviewed so that each review adds regression cases to the evaluation gate (M17).

mandatory.title: Safe platform upgrades
mandatory.requirement: Upgrade or roll back code, runtime, database schemas and configuration without corrupting existing work, approvals or business-effects records; zero downtime is a separate preference.

mandatory.title: Provider-independent deployability
mandatory.requirement: The composed solution must be viable self-hosted across appropriate on-premises/cloud environments, with no unavoidable single-provider SaaS; a fully offline run is a gate only for an air-gapped deployment profile.

mandatory.title: Enterprise and external-agent interoperability
mandatory.requirement: Integrate enterprise APIs and external agents through documented secured contracts with clear timeout/error handling and correlation. Tools exposed through MCP and agents exposing A2A must be consumable, natively or through a gateway, under the same identity and policy controls; native MCP/A2A support and broker plugins are preferences (H03, H07).

mandatory.title: Tenant safety where used
mandatory.requirement: Support single-tenant operation; when multi-tenancy is enabled, enforce identity, task/history, state, secret, memory and telemetry isolation across tenants. Do not mandate dynamic tenant-mode switching.

mandatory.title: Reproducible authoring and testable artifacts
mandatory.requirement: Reusable process/agent definitions, contracts and agent configurations must be accessible as versioned, inspectable artifacts that can be validated, tested, reviewed and delivered through a reproducible lifecycle. An IDE, visual editor or separate Development server is not mandatory.

mandatory.title: Separation of authority
mandatory.requirement: Authoring, production change approval and execution actions must have separable, enforceable privileges with attributable transitions. No particular two-/three-plane physical deployment, shared database or separately deployed control service is required.

mandatory.title: Safe autonomy during administration outages
mandatory.requirement: Execution and recovery must not depend on a live authoring or administration interface; continue on last approved state within a bounded freshness policy and fail closed for operations requiring fresh authorization or emergency revocation.

mandatory.title: Recoverable canonical progress and reconciliation
mandatory.requirement: For every running unit of work there must be one clear authoritative progress/state model with queryable task status, dependency and outcome evidence; any replicas, projections or multiple runtimes must reconcile correctly after crashes. A universal stand-alone task-ledger database is not required.

mandatory.title: Goal-driven planning and adaptive execution
mandatory.requirement: Agents can take a business goal, decompose it into steps at runtime, choose among permitted tools and sub-agents, and re-plan when a step fails or new information arrives, within the bounds of M02 and with every plan and plan change recorded (M15).

mandatory.title: Tool, knowledge and unstructured-input use
mandatory.requirement: Agents call registered tools (including MCP tools through M23), retrieve enterprise knowledge with source provenance and access control, and work from unstructured inputs such as documents, e-mails and conversations, with structured, validated outputs (M14).

mandatory.title: Multi-agent collaboration and delegation
mandatory.requirement: Agents hand off, delegate to and supervise other agents (internal or through A2A) with explicit task context, the delegating user's scoped authority (M11) and a shared view of task progress (M28); loops and circular delegation are bounded (M02).

mandatory.title: Interactive human-agent collaboration
mandatory.requirement: People converse with agents, see progress as it streams, answer clarifying questions, correct or redirect a running agent and take over a task; an agent can pause durably for human input and resume with the answer (M03, M05).

mandatory.title: Agent quality monitoring in production
mandatory.requirement: Agent outputs and trajectories are evaluated continuously in production (sampled automatic evaluation, user feedback and human review queues) against agreed quality criteria, with alerts and a path to the evaluation gate (M17) and containment (M20). Advanced analytics stay High priority (H13).

mandatory.title: Model choice and routing per agent task
mandatory.requirement: Each agent task can use a model chosen from approved providers, including self-hosted models, by configuration rather than code change, with routing by task type, risk tier or cost, and consistent evaluation (M17) of every model used.

high.title: Open Workflow Specification alignment
high.requirement: Prefer full authoring/import/export and verified semantic conformance to current OWS; model vendor extensions and round-trip loss.

high.title: Runtime and framework independence
high.requirement: Reduce engine and agent-framework lock-in through documented adapters, usable process and agent artifacts and substitutable service contracts; model choice itself is Mandatory (M34).

high.title: Native MCP and A2A support
high.requirement: Prefer native, secured MCP and A2A interoperability instead of only custom REST adapters.

high.title: High-volume scaling
high.requirement: Support large numbers of concurrent/waiting processes, agents and due timers with measurable horizontal scale beyond minimum recovery guarantees.

high.title: Administration and business task UI
high.requirement: Useful operator console and approver inbox over stable APIs; not mandatory for engine eligibility.

high.title: Advanced AI explanations
high.requirement: Auditable and reviewer-facing reasons, confidence, alternatives and explanations beyond ordinary decision provenance; mandatory only where an agreed risk/legal profile requires them.

high.title: Event broker integration
high.requirement: Prefer first-class Kafka and compatible messaging, reliable subscriptions and event-to-process correlation.

high.title: Advanced replay and simulation
high.requirement: Support historical deterministic replay and safe what-if runs including bounded model/tool fixture replay.

high.title: Advanced cost and model-usage governance
high.requirement: Usage/cost/latency budgets, estimation, attribution and optimization beyond the required hard per-task safety limits.

high.title: Automatic in-flight definition migration
high.requirement: Optional mapped migration to newer definitions with rollback and proof; correct version pinning remains Mandatory.

high.title: Zero-downtime upgrade
high.requirement: Achieve rolling upgrade availability SLO beyond required correctness of upgrade and rollback.

high.title: Developer lifecycle and packaging UX
high.requirement: Reusable templates, test fixtures, contract validation, CI promotion, dependency inventory and developer APIs beyond baseline versioned artifact validation.

high.title: Advanced AI quality analytics
high.requirement: Drift detection, prompt and model A/B comparison, trajectory analytics and quality dashboards beyond the mandatory production monitoring (M33).

high.title: Advanced scheduling calendars
high.requirement: Complex calendar rules, schedule optimization, extreme timer volumes and timezone-safe business calendars beyond durable due dates.

high.title: Strong workload isolation and cells
high.requirement: Isolate busy/failed tenants, runtimes and risk tiers with quotas, bulkheads or separate cells when the target scale warrants it.

high.title: Advanced tenancy administration
high.requirement: Self-service provisioning, quotas and guided migration between single and multi-tenant deployments where needed.

high.title: Dynamic activation
high.requirement: Apply more categories of approved changes without binary rebuild or workload restart, within controlled activation and version-safety rules.

high.title: AI-specific incident and red-team operations
high.requirement: Automated AI incident triage and continuing adversarial (red-team) tests beyond the mandatory containment and incident handling (M20) and the evaluation gate (M17).

high.title: Legacy transition and coexistence
high.requirement: Shadow runs, reversible cutover, cohort migration, reconciliation and independent completion of old instances in modernization programs.

high.title: Multilingual experience
high.requirement: Approvals, messages and explanations in languages actually served, with language-specific evaluation; may become a profile gate.

high.title: Multiple execution runtimes
high.requirement: Consistent governance and observable task state for separate process/agent runtimes, if justified by matched scenarios.

high.title: Visual/non-developer authoring
high.requirement: Allow process analysts to create, simulate and review workflows and agents through a visual UI or safe natural-language copilot, under the same approval controls.

high.title: Open-source licensing and reuse freedom
high.requirement: Prefer permissively licensed, auditable and redistributable open-source components with no mandatory managed-provider or commercial-production lock-in; score any license, support or redistribution restrictions and their total cost.

high.title: Simple, clean and maintainable architecture
high.requirement: Prefer cohesive abstractions, inspectable implementation, minimal bespoke framework code and infrastructure, low operating footprint, reproducible builds and long-term maintainability; score real implementation and support effort.

high.title: Long-term agent memory and personalization
high.requirement: Agents keep scoped, consented long-term memory of users and cases across sessions, with provenance, retention and erasure (M19), to improve continuity and personalization.

optional.title: Embedded governance assistant
optional.requirement: AI-assisted explanation, incident investigation and change proposals in an operator console; mandatory authorization constraints apply only when enabled.

optional.title: Separate hosted Development Plane
optional.requirement: Independent authoring portal/backend/deployment; only justified when authorship scale, tenant boundaries or team organization require it.

optional.title: Physical cell-based architecture
optional.requirement: Physical deployment cells, beyond performance isolation requirements; only when isolation/scale evidence justifies operational overhead.

optional.title: Full hot-swap without restart
optional.requirement: Universal dynamic swapping of all artifact types; useful only when lifecycle costs justify it.

optional.title: Full custom orchestration engine
optional.requirement: Building distributed scheduler, journal, coordination and process interpreter in-house rather than reusing proven components.

profiles.name: Air-gapped
profiles.effect: Offline artifact/image/model/credential dependency closure and offline execution under M22

profiles.name: Multi-tenant
profiles.effect: M24 tenant isolation across state, agent memory, secrets, logs, keys and operational APIs
profiles.activation: Deployment hosts more than one security tenant

profiles.name: High-impact decisions
profiles.effect: Extra oversight, reviewer explanations (H06) and appeal pathways as required by approved internal policy or law
profiles.activation: Process has legal or similarly significant consequences

profiles.name: UAE data protection
profiles.effect: Data subject rights, residency/transfer and retention policy gates in M13
profiles.activation: Applicable UAE personal-data legislation confirmed by Legal

profiles.name: Dubai Government
profiles.effect: Applicable DESC governance and Arabic/English support (H20) only where policy requires it

profiles.name: EU AI Act scope
profiles.effect: Additional role/risk-specific record keeping, oversight and explanation controls validated by Legal
profiles.activation: Specific EU jurisdiction and application scope applies

scenarios.title: Governed augmentation of an existing service
scenarios.purpose: Existing business process uses an AI evidence-review step, deterministic policy, authorized human action and idempotent fulfilment.

tests.description: Reject malformed agent output, forbidden action and unauthorized escalation
Prove authorized human task cannot be approved by a forbidden initiator/agent
Prove compensation and no duplicate side effect after acknowledgment loss
Trace every decision to actor, model/prompt/tool versions, and workflow step
Demonstrate existing enterprise-service adapters and timeout contracts, and consume an MCP tool and an A2A agent natively or through a gateway

scenarios.title: Bounded multi-agent task
scenarios.purpose: Agent delegation, bounded iterative plans, tools and memory; secure resume and emergency stop.

tests.description: Stop loops at agreed time, iteration, cost and tool limits
Reject agent-to-agent scope widening and expired/replayed delegated tokens
Restart during partial agent work; preserve progress, scoped memory and exactly one business effect
Inject prompt/tool-result attacks and prohibited sandbox access
Demonstrate model/tool provenance, the AI inventory with owner and risk tier, rejection of an uninventoried tool endpoint, and the quality-evaluation gate
Revoke a named agent/model/tool across active and waiting tasks; record, classify and report the incident and add a regression case to the evaluation suite

scenarios.title: Long-running process with approval and timers
scenarios.purpose: Weeks-long wait, due timer, event correlation, definition pinning and restart/restore.

tests.description: Pod/node failover while awaiting human action or due timer; deliver intended outcome once
Duplicate/late external events, cancellation race and failed compensation
Safe config/model/definition v1 continuation through v2 rollout and rollback
Recover reauthorized delegated identity and correctly-scoped memory
Inspect, cancel and retry individual tasks through authorized operations

scenarios.title: Operations, security and deployment
scenarios.purpose: Production failure, backup/restore, tenancy, model routing, publisher outage and emergency revocation.

tests.description: Demonstrate overload/backpressure and no committed progress corruption
Restore state, history, approvals and audit within agreed objectives
Authorized staged publication, secret rotation, rollback and recorded evidence
Prove location-constrained encryption, retention, erase and tenant boundary
Deployed in multiple self-hosted environments; offline under P1
Kill console/control services and prove controlled continuation/recovery with bounded staleness
Revoke policies and enforce fail-closed regardless of control service outage
Zero-data-loss upgrade/rollback for engine, schema and API in-flight

scenarios.title: Agent-generated bounded plan
scenarios.purpose: An agent constructs and revises an approved runtime plan; no silent promotion to reusable product configuration.

tests.description: Constrain dynamic plan to approved tools and policy and reject circular delegation
Crash after partial plan, preserve task state and effect-safety

scenarios.title: Modernization and coexistence
scenarios.purpose: Deploy behind legacy facade, compare shadow decisions, switch cohort, reverse safely and preserve old instances.

tests.description: Shadow execution never causes live side effects; reconciliation and rollback work
Existing versions finish while new versions activate and a release rollback occurs

scenarios.title: Design-to-production lifecycle
scenarios.purpose: Build and simulate versioned workflow and agent artifacts; approve safe rollout; deny unauthorised authoring-to-execution shortcuts.

tests.description: Validate, simulate, test and reproduce development artifact definition/prompt/tool dependencies
Unauthorized developer, agent or operator cannot activate/revoke protected production policy
Approve evaluated release, verify integrity and rollback with audit and incident containment
Execution remains independent of the authoring/administration UI on a pinned version
Runtime-generated agent plan cannot become production definition without controlled promotion

scenarios.title: Agent-led case resolution
scenarios.purpose: An agent takes an unstructured customer request, plans the resolution, retrieves policy knowledge, calls tools, delegates to specialist agents, converses with the customer and a case officer, and uses deterministic workflow steps only where a business guarantee needs them.

tests.description: From an unstructured request the agent builds a plan, executes it with permitted tools and re-plans after an injected tool failure, with every plan version recorded
The agent answers from enterprise knowledge with source citations, respects document permissions and turns an e-mail attachment into a validated structured record
A supervisor agent delegates to two specialist agents, one through A2A, passing scoped authority; a circular delegation is stopped and task progress is visible in one place
The customer and a case officer converse with the running agent, answer a clarifying question after a restart, redirect it, and the officer takes over the task
Sampled production evaluation and user feedback flag a quality drop, raise an alert and open an evaluation-gate review and containment
The same agent task switches between two approved providers and a self-hosted model by configuration and routes by risk tier; each model has evaluation evidence

principles: Select outcomes and evidence before implementation strategy
Three logical responsibilities do not imply three deployed planes
Production promotion and execution authorization must be non-bypassable
Durability, effect safety and progress consistency are independent guarantees
A versioned OWS artifact is preferred, but not a Mandatory technology choice
Existing runtime state can be authoritative; no universal physical task-ledger mandate
Security controls are mandatory for capabilities deployed, not a mandate to deploy optional capabilities
Open source and avoidance of provider lock-in must be transparently scored
Agentic capability is the reason for the solution: agents must be able to plan, use tools and knowledge, collaborate and converse, and workflow guarantees bound them rather than replace them

decisions.decision: Recognize authoring and reproducible lifecycle as logical responsibility, not a new deployment requirement
One canonical execution progress model with crash-safe reconciliation, not one mandatory global database
Accept suitable versioned, verified and audited publication; no prescribed signature transport
UI assistant optional; when used all agent operations must be authorized and audited
Strong High Priority scored dimensions, not automatic mandatory exclusions

decisions.topic: Gaps closed in review of 18 October
decisions.decision: AI inventory added to M18, minimal AI incident handling added to M20, MCP and A2A consumability (native or through a gateway) added to M23; transition and multiple runtimes stay High Priority because S6 tests and M28 already gate their safety
Add six Mandatory agentic capability outcomes (M29 to M34), one scenario (S8) and six tests; promote minimum production quality monitoring and model choice; add long-term memory as High priority
